note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Layer dropout configuration to training savings and inference elasticity

nodes.name: Dropout abandoned in LLM pretraining
nodes.description: As LLMs scaled to billions of parameters and trillions of tokens, dropout has largely disappeared from pretraining recipes, since single-epoch training on massive data leaves little room for classical overfitting and activation dropout is reported to degrade performance there.

nodes.name: Layer dropout gives structured sparsity
nodes.description: Skipping entire transformer blocks (layer dropout / stochastic depth) yields structured sparsity that reduces active training FLOPs almost linearly with the dropout rate and encourages robustness to reduced-depth execution at inference.

nodes.name: Prior degradations may reflect poor configuration
nodes.description: Reported accuracy degradation from layer dropout in decoder-only LLMs may come from suboptimal schedules or hyperparameters rather than fundamental limits, because no controlled large-scale study had varied these systematically.

nodes.name: Whole-block dropout beats sub-layer dropout
nodes.description: Layer dropout that drops whole transformer blocks per sample yields higher accuracy than sub-layer dropout that drops attention and FFN sub-blocks separately (Finding 1, Table 1).

nodes.name: Per-sequence beats per-batch dropout
nodes.description: For any given layer dropout rate, dropping per sequence yields lower loss than dropping per batch (Finding 2).

nodes.name: Non-uniform distribution across layers is better
nodes.description: For the same training FLOPs, a non-uniform dropout distribution across layers beats uniform; the Increasing Layer Distribution (ILD, rate rising linearly from 0 at the first layer) is recommended as the model scales (Finding 3).

nodes.name: Decaying time schedule is best
nodes.description: For a fixed training FLOPs budget, a schedule decaying from a maximum rate to zero (DTS) achieves the highest accuracy, outperforming constant and increasing schedules at all scales (Finding 4).

nodes.name: Recommended recipe
nodes.description: The recommended layer dropout practice is increasing dropout across layers and decreasing dropout across time, which gives the best accuracy for a given training FLOPs budget (Key takeaway 1).

nodes.name: Same-FLOPs loss improves, up to 25% FLOPs saved
nodes.description: With optimal layer distribution, time schedule and optimizer hyperparameters, layer dropout gives lower loss at the same training FLOPs, or similar validation loss while saving up to 25% of training FLOPs.

nodes.name: Dropout improves early-exit loss
nodes.description: Pretraining with layer dropout saves training FLOPs and always leads to better early-exit loss at inference; the decreasing schedule gives the lowest validation loss with competitive early-exit loss (Key takeaway 2, Finding 5).

nodes.name: Average dropout rate predicts zero-shot robustness
nodes.description: The average training dropout rate predicts zero-shot robustness to early exit and layer skipping without retraining, so a larger model degrades gracefully toward smaller-model performance when layers are skipped (Finding 6, Key takeaway 3).

nodes.name: Hero runs: up to 1.55x speedup
nodes.description: At 1.8B-8.2B scale, aggressive layer dropout (p_max=0.99) saves up to 25% of cumulative training FLOPs while largely preserving baseline generalization, enabling zero-shot inference speedups up to 1.55x (Key takeaway 4).

nodes.name: Self-speculative decoding speedup
nodes.description: Layer-dropout-trained models enable post-training optimizations such as self-speculative decoding, yielding up to 1.5x inference speedup with negligible accuracy loss.

isolated_nodes.name: Scope limited to structured depth-wise dropout
isolated_nodes.description: The study covers only structured depth-wise dropout (stochastic removal of whole transformer blocks), not neuron-level or weight-level dropout.

isolated_nodes.name: Scale of experiments
isolated_nodes.description: The study comprises more than 2400 pretraining experiments spanning 271M to 8.2B parameters and datasets up to 160B tokens, run on Cerebras CS-3 systems.

structural_reasoning: Prior-art gap leads to systematic ablations over granularity, sampling unit, distribution and schedule, producing a recipe whose benefits extend to inference elasticity and speedups.
